case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
Client Status & Housing

Client is currently in Week 3 of the Turn 90 program.
Client transitioned out of his mother’s residence and into a transitional house (managed by "Jen" at $225/week, deposit waived due to prior payment) to secure a quieter environment and consistent sleep, as his mother’s home was disruptive.
Reports getting along well with his new roommate.
Utilizing Uber and walking for transportation to the program.
Employment & Education

Current Job Search: Client expressed significant frustration regarding repeated employment denials following background checks (e.g., Lowe's, Pizza Hut, a downtown restaurant near USC) despite successful interviews. He has submitted applications to Food Lion and Church's Chicken and is awaiting DoorDash background check results (expected by the 24th) with plans to deliver via e-bike.
Program Placement & Training: Case manager reassured client that Turn 90's employment partners trust the program's referrals and discussed transitioning to active job placement in Week 4 (following next week's holiday schedule).
Certifications & GED: Case manager will schedule client (alongside peers) for forklift certification in approximately two weeks. Client noted that needing to pass the math portion is the final requirement for his GED. Case manager will send adult education contact information so client can inquire about pulling his transcripts from Irmo High and retaking the math test. Client was also informed about upcoming WIN assessments as an alternative credential for employers.
Legal, Financial & Barriers

Driver's License: Client has an ID, but his driver's license is suspended. Discussed obtaining a DMV printout of all outstanding tickets and reinstatement fees to create a clearance plan, utilizing internal program funds and a referral to the Rainy Day Fund (up to $750) once the total balance is brought below that threshold.
Financial Stress & Benefits: Client is experiencing high financial stress regarding phone bills, upcoming holiday expenses, and a recent cut to his SNAP benefits (~$300/month). He has applied for disability benefits based on a two-year history of severe depression and has completed initial intake phone calls.
Criminal Justice / Monitoring: Client has a Tuesday morning appointment (9:15 AM) for court-mandated administrative monitoring/testing. He confirmed he holds documentation showing his monitoring fees are supposed to be waived.
Mental Health & Behavioral Observations

Client presented with feelings of discouragement, financial pressure, and temptation to return to illegal income sources ("selling dope") to relieve immediate financial strain.
Protective Factors: Client demonstrated strong resilience and commitment to remaining free, citing his relationship with his 17-year-old daughter and his desire to be a positive role model and provider for his young sons (ages 3, 5, and 8).
Mental Health Treatment: Client is actively engaged with Columbia Area Mental Health and is compliant with his prescribed medications (Zoloft, Abilify, and Remeron) to manage depression, mood swings, sleep, and appetite.
Workplace Readiness: Discussed managing anger, impulsivity, and authority triggers on the job. Client acknowledged a quick temper when feeling disrespected or criticized at work, and engaged in brief cognitive reframing/role-play around tolerating workplace frustration to maintain employment and long-term financial stability.
Action Plan & Next Steps

Client: Attend Tuesday 9:15 AM monitoring appointment and return to the program in the afternoon to avoid missing a full day.
Client: Visit the DMV to obtain the official printout of all tickets and reinstatement fees.
Client: Maintain full attendance on Wednesday and the following Monday to ensure holiday pay eligibility.
Case Manager: Send adult education contact information to client to assist with GED math test scheduling and transcript retrieval.
Case Manager: Coordinate with staff in Charleston to schedule client's forklift certification after next week.
Case Manager: Begin active job placement outreach with client in Week 4 and initiate Rainy Day Fund referral once DMV printout is reviewed.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
1. Topics Covered & Information Gathered
Employment & Background:
Client expressed urgency to secure employment and discussed applying independently through staffing agencies (e.g., Automation Personnel Services) and directly (e.g., International Paper on Bush River Rd).
Reviewed program timeline: Reentry cohort job placement typically initiates around Week 4 to allow foundational stability (licensing, identification, medical, stability milestones). Case Manager emphasized the value of program employer partnerships and advocacy recommendations in overcoming background check barriers.
Client disclosed legal history: convictions for Domestic Violence (DV 1, DV 2) from roughly 2023–2024, noting past releases and recent release on December 31st. Client noted awareness of how DV convictions complicate hiring.
Cognitive-Behavioral & Mindset Discussion:
Explored client’s focus on practicing patience, impulse control, and managing internal self-talk.
Discussed locus of control: shifting attention away from past charges/uncontrollable outcomes toward daily controllables (professional presentation, communication, punctuality).
Client articulated a firm commitment to maintaining freedom ("Nothing is worth my freedom") and recognized past incarceration patterns were becoming dangerously normalized. Client discussed redefining his protective role as a father/family provider through positive modeling rather than physical conflict.
Education & Skill Development:
Completed multiple certifications via SkillCat (HVAC, Welding, Electrician, Plumbing).
Client noted that while the classroom portion involves substantial reading and covers material he previously encountered in court-mandated DV classes, he views it as a valuable refresher. Client highlighted hands-on technical skills and mechanical aptitude.
Entrepreneurship & Financial Goals:
Client maintains an active LLC for landscaping/hardscaping and has developed a draft $100,000 business loan proposal packet.
Discussed establishing banking: Client plans to open business and personal checking/savings accounts in person at AllSouth Federal Credit Union.
Housing & Stability:
Client is transitioning from living with family to independent/transitional living to foster autonomy, establish personal space, build savings habits, and reduce household friction.
Resume Revision:
Reviewed and updated employment chronology with specific month/year ranges for Indeed job matching:
Freddy’s: July 2023
Arby’s: Closing Manager / Crew Member (Lake Murray & Irmo locations; 2019–2020, 2023)
Universal Cleaning Specialties: April 2016 – August 2022 (approx. 6 years)
Jimmy John’s: February 2015 – May 2015
KFC: December 2014 – February 2015
Car Wash Attendant: August 2007 – March 2008 (post-Job Corps)
2. Assessment
Client is highly motivated to work and demonstrates self-initiative, completing trade certifications and pursuing business planning independently.
Restlessness and financial pressure are creating some impatience regarding the structured 8-week timeline. Client was receptive to cognitive reframing regarding program milestones and partnership placement advantages.
Shows solid self-awareness regarding past behavioral triggers and the necessity of breaking institutionalization habits.
3. Plan & Action Items
Case Manager:
Finalize and print updated professional resume with detailed employment dates and highlight SkillCat certifications (HVAC, Welding, Electrical, Plumbing) at the top of the resume prior to tomorrow morning's session.
Assist client with uploading the finalized resume to Indeed.
Client:
Continue attendance and participation in daily cohort programming (9:00 AM – 3:00 PM).
Visit AllSouth Federal Credit Union branch to open business and personal banking accounts.
Continue steps toward transitional housing move-in.
Next Contact: Daily cohort check-in tomorrow morning at class start.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
1. Education & Goals
90-Day Goal: Obtain GED.
History & Next Steps: Client previously took the test in high school (did not pass math). Client identified a free Saturday GED program in Lexington and has the contact number saved. Case manager and client agreed to collaborate on enrollment and prep steps.
2. Legal, Supervision, & Licensing
Supervision Status: Client completed active supervision/paperwork six months post-release (June) and is currently on administrative monitoring due to outstanding courthouse fines/fees. Client reports the public defender’s office indicated these may be forgivable and is awaiting written confirmation via email.
Driver’s License: Client has 19 reinstatement fees and outstanding court tickets/fines across multiple jurisdictions (e.g., Lexington County, City of Columbia).
Recommendation: Case manager advised client to visit the DMV to obtain a full printed breakdown of all citations and fees to establish an organized payoff and reinstatement plan.
3. Employment & Transportation
Work History & Current Search: Client has experience in food service, car washes, temporary labor (Hire Quest), and informal automotive repair/landscaping. Client is actively seeking full-time work ($15+/hour) and has applied to various local employers (e.g., Sysco, Walmart, Ace Hardware, and food service).
Leads Discussed: International Paper (requires GED or active progress) and Aspire Bakeries (West Columbia, entry-level production/cookie plant).
Transportation: Client primarily utilizes Uber, public transit (bus), or walks to commute. Client showed high determination regarding transit, planning to use Uber/bus connections for prospective shifts.
4. Housing & Basic Needs
Current Living Situation: Client is currently staying with their mother.
Transitional Housing Referrals: Client expressed a strong desire for independent housing. Case manager provided contact details for two options:
Contact info for independent landlady ("Ms. Jean").
311 Living Solutions (Two Notch area): Shared rooms ($700/mo) and private rooms ($850/mo), furnished with utilities, laundry, and Wi-Fi included.
Identification & Health: Client confirmed possession of State ID, Social Security card, and birth certificate. Client receives needed maintenance medications at no cost via Well Vista mail-order delivery. Client has no child support orders.
5. Action Plan & Next Steps
Client Tasks:
Contact the housing providers (Ms. Jean and 311 Living Solutions) to check availability and application criteria.
Visit the local DMV branch to obtain a comprehensive driving record and fee/ticket breakdown.
Call the Lexington adult education contact regarding Saturday GED placement testing.
Case Manager Tasks:
Provide contact and application details for Aspire Bakeries and assist with ongoing job applications.
Follow up on GED enrollment progress and license resolution steps during the next scheduled check-in.

case_notes.content: Robert came in to check his status to enroll in First Shift. He passed a preliminary drug test and was scheduled for orientation on 6/22. He was reminded he will need to pass a drug test on orientation and weekly thereafter. At the end of the conversation, Robert informed me he is in need of emergency housing. I contacted Greyce Transitional home who is willing to accept and do a payment plan for him pending enrollment in T90.

Released from SCDC on Dec 31, 2025 and has not found a job since then. Has applied at fast food, warehouses, WalMart, Amazon, etc. with no return call. His VM is set up and checks his email regularly. Stays with his mother and although he is grateful, he wants his own place. Has four children and is not on child support. Does not have DL, has $1900 in reinstatement fees alone, and does not know how much he owes in tickets.  Will refer to RDF after gathering ticket info. Explained the First Shift program and reviewed eligibility for enrollment. He is usure if he can pass a drug test at this time but will test himself and follow up with me.
Rescheduled appointment twice. 6/9 is the most recently scheduled intake.
